text:
Predicates:
RankedHighly(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is among the most active players in major tennis.
LostTo(x, y) ::: x lost to y.
FemalePlayerRG2022(x) ::: x is a female tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
MalePlayerRG2022(x) ::: x is a male tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.
Player(x) ::: x is a player.

Premises:
∀x (RankedHighly(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: If a player is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association, then they are among the most active players in major tennis.
∀x (LostTo(x, iga) → RankedHighly(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
∀x (FemalePlayerRG2022(x) → LostTo(x, iga)) ::: All female tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
∀x (FemalePlayerRG2022(x) ∨ MalePlayerRG2022(x)) ::: Either female tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 or male tennis players at Roland Garros 2022.
∀x (MalePlayerRG2022(x) → LostTo(x, nadal)) ::: All male tennis players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
(RankedHighly(coco) ∨ LostTo(coco, nadal)) → ¬MalePlayerRG2022(coco) ::: If Coco Gauff is a player who is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association or a player who lost to Rafael Nadal, then Coco Gauff is not a male tennis player at Roland Garros 2022.

Conclusion:
LostTo(coco, nadal) ::: Coco Gauff has lost to Rafael Nadal.
